title: Test a taught word somewhere new
statement: A check on a taught word must put it in a new situation, because a key that repeats the teaching example can be picked from memory without knowing the meaning.
example: In four lessons the key of a word check copied or nearly copied the teaching card's own example.
detail: Hand reviews of four reading lessons found word checks whose keyed sentence copied or nearly copied the example on the word's teaching card, so a student could answer from memory of the card without knowing the word. In each case the fix the review proposed was a new situation for the key.

evidence.quote: A student can answer from memory of the card, without knowing what eerie means.
Memory of the example answers both, with no need to know the meaning.
This tests memory of the card, not the meaning.

The keyed stranger/shadows/cold-stare/slow-heavy-steps sentence closely copies p2's teaching example. That distinctive wording creates a recognition shortcut unrelated to applying the definition.
